stemBlocks.value: A straight line has gradient 3 and passes through the point (2, −4). Determine its equation in the form y = mx + c.
Think first: The gradient gives you m straight away; the point is there to pin down c.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p123-q07 from workbook page 123.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the equation with the known gradient.
Check the point satisfies the equation.

strategyBlocks.value: Write y = 3x + c, substitute the coordinates of the given point to find c, then state the full equation.

whyThisWorks.value: Infinitely many lines have gradient 3, and they differ only in the value of c — the height at which they cross the y-axis. Supplying one point the line must pass through selects exactly one of them, which is why substituting the coordinates determines c uniquely.

commonErrors.misconception: Substituting the point as x = −4, y = 2.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Substituting the point as x = −4, y = 2.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing c = 10 by moving 6 across without changing its sign.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing c = 10 by moving 6 across without changing its sign.

commonErrors.misconception: Leaving the answer as −4 = 3x + c instead of a finished equation.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Leaving the answer as −4 = 3x + c instead of a finished equation.

examTip.value: Always substitute your point back into the finished equation — a one-line check catches a sign slip in c.
